title: Kpler Data Shows Iran Has Lost Significant Control of the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Maritime intelligence firm Kpler found that more than 80% of liquids transits through the Strait of Hormuz over the prior two weeks took the UN-authorized Omani route -- which Iran opposes -- or were 'dark' transits likely also using that route, indicating Iran can no longer reliably charge tolls or control shipping through the strait it once dominated. President Trump reiterated a claim of US 'total control' of the strait, but analysts noted continued Iranian attacks and oil flows still well below pre-war levels mean neither side fully controls the waterway.

media.caption: Kpler data shows most Hormuz-bound traffic now avoids Iran's contested route in favor of the Omani corridor
